high.title: Ringgit retreats on Middle East concerns
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0930/4.0990 against the US dollar despite Malaysia's Q2 2026 GDP growth beating expectations at 5.8% versus the 5.3% consensus forecast. The stronger-than-expected GDP performance signals economic resilience amid global uncertainties, with full-year growth projected at around 5%. This combination of positive domestic fundamentals and external currency pressures is critical for investors monitoring forex and macroeconomic conditions.

high.title: Bursa higher at close on foreign fund inflows, second quarter GDP
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 9.26 points at 1,731.45, driven by foreign fund inflows and a stronger-than-expected Q2 2026 GDP result. Softer inflation and a stable overnight policy rate of 2.75% are supporting consumer spending and business investment. This market-moving session reflects improving sentiment among foreign investors towards Malaysian equities.

high.title: Bursa ends higher on broad-based buying
high.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 8.43 points (0.49%) to close at 1,722.19, supported by foreign fund inflows and selective buying in financial, plantation and industrial sectors. Investor sentiment was boosted by expectations that Malaysia's Q2 GDP will remain above 4%, with results due the following day. Wall Street's overnight gains from softer US wholesale inflation and strong bank earnings further reinforced expectations of Fed easing.

high.title: Ringgit rises as soft US data weighs on greenback
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0655/4.0710 against the USD as the US Dollar Index fell 0.43% following an unexpected 0.3% month-on-month decline in US PPI for June. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's testimony signalled no urgency to raise interest rates, lending support to emerging market currencies including the ringgit. Lower energy prices tied to the US-Iran ceasefire were a key driver of easing inflation pressures.

high.title: Bursa ends lower, weighed by profit-taking in banking, energy stocks
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed down 6.18 points at 1,713.76, driven by profit-taking in banking and energy sectors. Despite the headline decline, market breadth remained positive with healthcare, consumer and plantation stocks outperforming. Turnover expanded to 4.07 billion units valued at RM2.84 billion, indicating active market participation.

high.title: Ringgit opens higher ahead of Q2 GDP estimate
high.summary: The ringgit strengthened to 4.0740/4.0780 against the USD ahead of Malaysia's Q2 2026 advance GDP release on Friday. Economists forecast above 5% GDP growth at 5.1%, supported by strong E&E and commodity exports. However, cautious consumer spending may temper overall growth momentum.

high.title: Ringgit ends lower against US dollar amid cautious sentiment
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0760/4.0800 against the USD as traders awaited US June CPI data amid cautious sentiment. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and potential Strait of Hormuz disruptions elevated crude oil price risks, threatening renewed inflation acceleration. These external pressures weighed on investor risk appetite for emerging market assets including Malaysian equities.

high.title: Energy, banking stocks lift Bursa
high.summary: The FBM KLCI surged 21.50 points (1.26%) to close at 1,719.94, driven by energy and banking stocks amid escalating US-Iran tensions and rising crude oil prices. Commodity-linked stocks and Malaysia's defensive sector composition helped Bursa outperform regional peers. This represents a significant single-day rally with clear geopolitical catalysts affecting investor positioning.

high.title: Bursa opens higher on healthcare, property buying
high.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened higher as US-Iran tensions escalated, with Trump declaring a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, causing Brent crude to spike to US$83 per barrel. The early market breadth was negative despite the index gain, signaling selective investor caution. This geopolitical development has direct implications for Malaysian energy stocks and broader market sentiment.

medium.title: Bursa opens slightly lower on profit taking
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI opened weaker amid profit-taking influenced by an overnight pullback in US semiconductor stocks, creating selling pressure in Malaysia's technology sector. However, optimism around the official launch of the Large Scale Solar 6 (LSS6) programme is expected to cushion downside risks and rotate buying interest toward renewable energy and energy storage plays. This is notable for investors tracking the local tech and green energy sectors.

medium.title: Ringgit flat against US dollar, higher versus major currencies
medium.summary: The ringgit was range-bound between RM4.06 and RM4.08 ahead of Malaysia's advance Q2 2026 GDP estimate, with analysts projecting growth of around 5.1% supported by strong E&E exports. The US Dollar Index edged higher as Fed officials maintained a hawkish stance on interest rates, adding pressure on the ringgit. This is relevant for businesses and investors exposed to currency risk and tracking monetary policy developments.

medium.title: Tesla plans production increase at Germany's Grünheide factory
medium.summary: Tesla plans to ramp up production at its German Grünheide plant to up to 7,500 vehicles per week while creating 3,500 new jobs and expanding battery cell production. The German unit posted net profit of €77.1 million for 2025, up ~€20 million year-on-year despite a challenging market. This is relevant to Malaysian investors with exposure to global EV supply chains and E&E export demand.

medium.title: Ringgit firms as US rate hike expectations recede
medium.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0710/4.0745 against the greenback by market close, supported by receding US rate hike expectations following softer-than-expected CPI and PPI data. Asian currencies were broadly firmer as the Fed chair indicated no rush to raise rates. However, the ringgit remained mostly lower against other major currencies.

medium.title: Bursa rebounds on stronger investor appetite
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 4.30 points to 1,718.06 in early trading, driven by improving global risk sentiment following softer US producer inflation data. Technology counters were highlighted as likely beneficiaries of selective buying interest. Wall Street's positive momentum was expected to extend into Bursa Malaysia's session.

medium.title: Ringgit ends flat against US dollar
medium.summary: The ringgit closed flat at 4.0760/4.0805 against the USD despite lower-than-expected US CPI, as market focus shifted to China's slowing Q2 GDP growth of 4.3%, down from 5% in Q1. Fragility in the Middle East ceasefire added to cautious sentiment. The ringgit also traded mostly lower against a basket of major currencies.

medium.title: Bursa gains on improved sentiment ahead of GDP data
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI rose 3.15 points to 1,723.09 in early trade, buoyed by a Wall Street rebound led by semiconductor stocks. Weaker-than-expected US June inflation data eased Federal Reserve rate hike concerns, pushing the US 10-year Treasury yield down to 4.587%. Positive external sentiment and upcoming domestic GDP data provided a constructive backdrop for Malaysian equities.

medium.title: Syahrul Azmir made new CEO of Rapid Bus
medium.summary: Rapid Bus appointed Syahrul Azmir as its new CEO, bringing over 27 years of logistics and transport sector experience. The appointment aligns with Rapid Bus's strategic push to expand electric bus deployment and improve service reliability across Rapid KL and Rapid Penang networks. This leadership change signals continued investment in Malaysia's public transport infrastructure and sustainability goals.
